Can Composio build a toolkit for it? 100 apps, researched by an agent

An agent read each app's own docs and decided how it authenticates, whether a developer can get credentials alone, how big the API is, whether an MCP server exists, and whether a toolkit could ship today. Every answer quotes the docs page behind it. The whole dataset went through 3 automated verification loops, and a stratified sample was then audited for accuracy.

58ready today
36ready with caveats
6blocked
74%self-serve credentials
74%support OAuth2
81% → 83%accuracy, pass 1 → final (AI-audited sample, not human)

The patterns

  1. Static keys/tokens are the most common auth: 77 of 100 apps accept an API key or token, 74 support OAuth2, and 56 offer both - so most toolkits can start on API-key auth and add OAuth for multi-tenant use.
  2. Getting credentials is mostly self-serve: 74% of apps let a developer get working credentials alone (free or trial); 19 are gated by an admin, app review, partner programme or sales.
  3. Gating clusters by category: Developer, Infra and Data platforms is the most self-serve (100%), Marketing, Ads, Email and Social the least (40%).
  4. The most common blocker is 'paid plan' (13 apps); 58 apps are ready today, 36 ready with caveats, 6 blocked.
  5. MCP is already mainstream: at least 50 vendors ship an official MCP server and 25 more have community servers (a lower bound - the accuracy audit shows the agent misses official MCP servers more than anything else).
  6. Composio already has toolkits for 80 of the 100; 4 self-serve, ready apps have no Composio toolkit yet - the cheapest net-new wins.

The agent

1 · DiscoverHint URLs + model-proposed official URLs (Claude WebSearch for the first 38 apps) + GitHub MCP search + Composio's public toolkit catalog, then a one-hop crawl for auth/pricing/MCP links.
→
2 · Fetch & cachePolite HTTP fetch (UA, 1 req/s per host); every page cached with a timestamp. That cache is the only allowed evidence source.
→
3 · Extract (pass 1)A fast model (Claude Haiku) fills the schema from the cached pages and must quote the page for each answer. Snapshot kept as pass1.
→
4 · Loop 1Code-only checks: quote exists in the page, URL returned 200, enum/schema valid, consistency rules, Composio catalog cross-check.
→
5 · Loop 2An independent second agent re-researches each app blind to pass 1; field-level disagreements are flagged.
→
6 · Loop 3Headless Chromium re-renders flagged and JS-built pages; Claude Sonnet adjudicates with fresh quotes, which are re-checked in code.
→
7 · Accuracy auditStratified sample (fixed seed, 260 field checks). A human review tool was built, but the hand check was skipped for time, so an independent AI auditor (Claude Opus) judged it, and the page says so.

Plain Python, about 1,500 lines. LLM calls go through one wrapper that can use the local claude CLI or the Anthropic API. This run: 482 logged LLM stage calls, about $32 list-price equivalent. Composio is used through its public toolkit catalog (no key needed), with an optional SDK check (Composio().toolkits.get) when COMPOSIO_API_KEY is set.

Loop 1 · deterministic

918 evidence quotes checked against the cached pages: 87.1% verified (605 exact, 195 re-anchored to the page's own wording), 118 dropped. 19 field values downgraded to unknown because no quote survived. Rule flags: definitional_verdict x6, evidence_gate x6, api_key_without_key_evidence x4, oauth2_without_oauth_evidence x3, composio_has_api_key_we_do_not x2, mcp_url_not_mcp_page x1, composio_has_oauth2_we_do_not x1, ready_without_api x1.

Loop 2 · independent second agent

Different discovery, prompt and URL model, blind to pass 1. Hard disagreements: mcp.official x28, buildability.main_blocker x25, buildability.verdict x22, auth.methods x6, access.status x5, api_surface.styles x3. 53 apps had at least one; 15 gaps filled with verified answers.

Loop 3 · headless browser + adjudicator

74 apps re-examined (151 fields) with pages rendered in Chromium; a stronger model decided each field with a fresh quote that was re-verified in code. 42 values changed; 23 left unresolved → sent to the human.

38 of 100 apps (38%) had at least one key value changed by the automated loops (access.status x14, buildability.verdict x14, buildability.main_blocker x13, mcp.official x10, auth.methods x5, api_surface.styles x3).

Proof: run it yourself

  • Source + README: https://github.com/karanLokhande29/composio-toolkit-research
  • Runnable trigger: GitHub Actions → “research” → Run workflow (choose app ids; verify-only mode needs no API keys and re-checks every evidence quote live against the vendor pages).
  • Locally: 
    python run.py --apps 1-5 --stage all
  • For agents: llms.txt · results.json · patterns.json · metrics.json; the full dataset is also embedded in this page as <script id="data">.

Process

  1. 15:40 · P0 setup — Read brief + MASTER; verified Composio docs (package `composio`, keyless public catalog); scaffolded repo, apps.yaml (100), checker
  2. 15:45 · P1 pilot — Apps 1-5: discover (WebSearch agent) -> extract (haiku) -> loop 1; R1-R8 PASS for pilot
  3. 15:51 · P2 scale — Claude CLI hit plan usage limit mid-discovery (apps 39-50 lost search results; discarded)
  4. 16:20 · P2 scale — Limit reset; switched apps 39-100 to cheap discovery (model-proposed URLs + crawl); parallel extraction
  5. 16:35 · P2 scale — Pass 1 complete for all 100 apps (3 parallel extraction processes, merge-safe saves)
  6. 16:46 · P3 loops — Loop 1 on all 100; Loop 2 second agent on all 100; then Claude plan usage limit hit again (reset 21:20)
  7. 21:31 · P3 loops — Loop 1 re-run with corrected MCP rule; Loop 2 re-applied from cache; Loop 3 browser + adjudicator on 74 flagged apps
  8. 21:55 · P4/P5 accuracy — Human hand-check skipped by Karan (time); independent AI auditor (Claude Opus) judged the 260-row stratified sample; labelled as such on the page
  9. 22:02 · P6-P8 — Patterns, page, deploy to GitHub Pages; MCP weakness reported honestly

Limitations and honest failures

  • Discovery depth varied by budget. Apps 1–38 used Claude's web search for discovery. After the CLI hit its usage limit, apps 39–100 used model-proposed URLs plus crawling, which has lower recall for obscure apps.
  • MCP is the weakest field and the loops made it worse. In the accuracy audit, MCP was the least accurate field, and it was the only one where accuracy dropped after the loops. The agent mostly misses official MCP servers (e.g. Google Ads, Supabase, Linear, Jira/Atlassian, Snowflake, Vercel). These are announced on pages the crawler never fetched, and Loop 3 dropped some correct ones because the URL wasn't quoted on a fetched page. Fix: add a dedicated MCP discovery step (vendor docs search plus the MCP registry) before extraction.
  • Docs say what's allowed, not what works. Without paid or partner accounts, gated apps are judged from public docs only (as the brief asks). Nothing was tested with live credentials.
  • Breadth is a judgement (narrow/moderate/broad), not an endpoint count. Composio-toolkit presence is an exact name match against Composio's public catalog, which can miss renamed toolkits.
  • Not SaaS: Sherlock (cli or library), Mermaid CLI (cli or library). These are classified as what they are, not forced into the SaaS mould.

  • Amazon Selling Partner: auth: loop1: no evidence snippet could be verified in the fetched pages; access: Pages show self-serve registration steps for sandbox and production, but do not explicitly document whether production app approval/review
  • fanbasis: auth: Page mentions APIs/SDKs exist but specifies no authentication methods, grant types, or technical details.; access: Enterprise APIs referenced without describing sandbox access, approval workflows, sign-up process,
  • Sherlock: auth: Not a hosted API: this is a CLI / open-source tool run locally, so no API authentication applies
  • Paygent Connect: auth: No pages provided; access: No pages provided; api_surface: No pages provided; mcp: No pages provided
  • higgsfield: auth: loop1: no evidence snippet could be verified in the fetched pages; access: Pages discuss credits-based pricing with per-request costs and mention plans, but do not explicitly state availability of free tier, free t
  • Mermaid CLI: auth: Not a hosted API: this is a CLI / open-source tool run locally, so no API authentication applies

Next steps: authenticated API probes for the self-serve apps (to confirm the auth answers end to end), a larger human sample, and wiring discovery through Composio's search tools once an API key is available.
